## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag breaks the project's CLI-flag policy because it has no `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment-variable default, so CI cannot set it. This is the only defect this review found, and it should be fixed.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect` now skips files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped path. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end tests, and adds a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs the tool, `.log` files are still archived, because the flag's default is the hard-coded `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot use exclusion, which is the reason the rule exists. — Fix: Derive the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple patterns, and add a test next to `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
